compiled_state.description:
## Finding

Found while reviewing the ADR 0117 draft (task `arterial-bilineate-vampirebat` /
`a01e-01e7-6e6e-4809`) against the tree. The draft cited `src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:33` as one of
three sibling modules that "already guard correctly", offered as evidence that `lock.py` is an
outlier. Re-reading the file shows the opposite: **`marker.py` has the identical defect.**

```
src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:9-11    try: import fcntl / except ImportError: fcntl = None
src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:33      fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)      # write_marker,  unguarded
src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:38      fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)      # write_marker,  unguarded
src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:61      fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)      # clear_marker,  unguarded
src/rebar/reducer/marker.py:67      fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)      # clear_marker,  unguarded
```

The import is guarded to `None`; the four uses are not. On Windows every one raises
`AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'`.

The two genuine counter-examples in the draft do hold — `_snapshot/git_fetch.py:79` and
`_snapshot/janitor.py:430` both branch on `if fcntl is not None` before use. `marker.py` was the
third citation and it is wrong.

## Why the surrounding `try/except OSError` does not contain it

Both functions wrap the locked region in `try: ... except OSError:` and log a warning, documented as
"On any OSError: logs a warning to stderr and returns without raising. Failed marker writes must not
prevent callers from proceeding." **`AttributeError` is not an `OSError`**, so it is not caught: it
propagates out of a function whose contract says it never raises. The `finally:` at `:37`/`:66` then
runs `fcntl.flock(lock_fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)`, which raises a *second* `AttributeError` from the
cleanup path and replaces the first.

So this is not merely "another Windows failure". It breaks a documented never-raises contract, and
it does so through the `finally` block, which is the shape that loses the original error.

## Relationship to S1

Separate from `S1` (`friendless-alabaster-cub`), which owns `_store/lock.py` and
`_store/lock_owner.py` and is actively in flight. This ticket must NOT touch those files. It is
listed under the same epic because it is the same root cause in a different module, and because
`S1`'s Windows exclusive-lock leg may supply the mechanism this file should call rather than
open-coding a second one.

Sequence after `S1`: reuse whatever guarded exclusive-lock helper `S1` lands rather than adding an
independent `if fcntl is not None` branch here, so the tree ends with one Windows locking mechanism
and not three.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

1. `write_marker` and `clear_marker` do not raise `AttributeError` when `fcntl is None`; a test
   proves it by patching `rebar.reducer.marker.fcntl` to `None`.
2. The documented never-raises contract holds under `fcntl is None` — the functions return normally,
   and the `finally` unlock path does not raise.
3. Serialization is still enforced on POSIX (the existing behaviour is unchanged when `fcntl` is
   available), proven by a test that still exercises the real lock.
4. Neither `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` nor `src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py` is modified.
